author: Team 1635
title: Building More Than Robots: How We Sparked a STEM Movement in Newtown H.S.
excerpt: How our robotics expo and the Future-Ready CTE program are breaking down barriers in STEM.
body:
It all started with a soaring ball, spinning wheels, and a robot on display.

Last year, our robotics team, Technotics, hosted a robotics expo where students could get an up-close look at how programming, engineering, and collaboration come together to turn an idea into reality.

It was hard to miss the vivacity of the tight-knit team, a bunch of high school students bursting with passion for STEM and creation. Standing proudly alongside them was Newtown’s very own FRC competition robot, AJ, built to shoot balls with precision and speed. Our veteran team members explained how the robot worked, the competitions they entered, how the club was structured, and the many exciting opportunities ahead. More than just showcasing a piece of machinery, though, the event gave interested students a chance to ask questions, explore new possibilities, and imagine themselves as future innovators.

For outsiders looking in, that single robotics expo changed everything. In fact, seeing that presentation is exactly what inspired new members—including myself—to join the team this year. All it takes is a single spark.

However, the ripple effects went far beyond our club roster. Our school recently implemented the Future-Ready CTE program, focusing directly on robotics and computer science. This initiative has given Newtown students vastly more opportunities to explore STEM, develop practical skills, and build confidence in their career paths through hands-on education.

It’s heartening to see robotics become accessible to those outside our team, introducing a whole new world to the broader student body.

That’s what makes these efforts so meaningful to Technotics. We are helping break down barriers in STEM exploration for high school students, emphasizing that you don’t have to know how to code, understand engineering, or have any prior experience to try something new. We focus on expanding STEM education and making a permanent impact on our school community, because the students gathered around our robot today could easily become tomorrow’s pioneers.

Through our outreach and classroom integration, Newtown is creating real opportunities for future generations of students to discover what they are capable of. Our team is dedicated to something bigger than winning a competitive season—we aim to inspire and encourage every single student at Newtown.

We build robots to compete, but the true goal is to inspire others to build them too. For Team Technotics, we are just getting started.
